title: Unit 3: Cells
description: Comprehensive questions covering Grade 9 Biology Unit 3: Cells, including cell theory, cell structure, types of cells, animal vs plant cells, microscopy, cell environment (diffusion, osmosis, active transport), and levels of biological organization.

questions.question: Who was the first scientist to observe cells and use the word 'cell'?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke observed thin slices of cork in 1665 and called the pore-like structures 'cells'.

questions.question: In which year did Robert Hooke first observe cells?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke observed cells in 1665 after examining thin slices of plant material (cork).

questions.question: Who is universally acknowledged as the father of microbiology?
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek discovered micro-organisms like protists and bacteria using his hand-built microscopes.

questions.question: Which German botanist stated that all plants are made up of cells?
questions.explanation: In 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, concluded that all plants are made up of cells.

questions.question: Which German zoologist reported that all animals are made up of cells?
questions.explanation: In 1839, Theodor Schwann reported that all animals are made up of cells, extending cell theory to animals.

questions.question: Who established the idea that cells arise only by the division of existing cells?
questions.explanation: In 1856, Rudolf Virchow, a German pathologist, established that cells arise only from pre-existing cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a principle of cell theory?
options: Living organisms are composed of one or more cells
Cells are the smallest unit of life
Cells can arise spontaneously from non-living matter
Cells arise only by the division of a pre-existing cell
questions.correctAnswer: Cells can arise spontaneously from non-living matter
questions.explanation: Cell theory states that cells arise only from pre-existing cells, not spontaneously.

questions.question: According to cell theory, cells arise only by the division of a:
questions.explanation: Rudolf Virchow established that all cells arise from pre-existing cells by division.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of life according to cell theory?
questions.explanation: Cell theory states that cells are the smallest unit of life that can carry out all life processes.

questions.question: Every living cell is surrounded by a membrane that separates the cell contents from the outside. This membrane is called the:
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane (cell membrane) surrounds every living cell and separates its contents from the external environment.

questions.question: Which organelle is described as the 'powerhouse' of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of respiration where energy is produced, hence called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.question: The largest organelle in most eukaryotic cells is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus is usually the largest organelle and contains the cell's genetic material (DNA).

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are small structures found in all cells that synthesize proteins.

questions.question: Ribosomes are found either freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes attach to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, giving it a dotted appearance.

questions.question: Rough endoplasmic reticulum gets its name from:
options: the ribosomes attached to its surface
questions.correctAnswer: the ribosomes attached to its surface
questions.explanation: The rough ER appears dotted because of ribosomes attached to its surface, giving it a 'rough' appearance.

questions.question: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is primarily involved in the manufacturing of:
questions.explanation: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is important for lipid manufacturing.

questions.question: Which organelle functions in the collection, packaging, and distribution of molecules within the cell?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages, and distributes proteins and lipids within or outside the cell.

questions.question: Small sacs that store and transport materials in the cell are called:
questions.explanation: Vesicles are small membranous sacs that store, transport, and ship materials within the cell.

questions.question: Which organelle contains digestive enzymes to break down bacteria and damaged organelles?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound packages of digestive enzymes that break down foreign matter and damaged organelles.

questions.question: Large vacuoles that occupy more than half of the cell volume are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Many plant cells have large central vacuoles that occupy more than half of the cell volume.

questions.question: Chloroplasts are the site for:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site where photosynthesis occurs in green plants.

questions.question: The green pigment found in chloroplasts that traps sunlight energy is called:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts that captures sunlight energy for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which structure provides rigid support and gives shape to plant cells?
questions.explanation: The cell wall is a rigid structure external to the cell membrane that provides structural support and shape.

questions.question: The cell wall of plant cells is primarily made of:
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are composed of cellulose, while bacterial cell walls are made of peptidoglycan.

questions.question: Animal cells do NOT have which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: Animal cells have no cell wall; cell walls are found in plant, fungal, and some bacterial cells.

questions.question: Prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells mainly because they lack:
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles, unlike eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a prokaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes; they lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: Eukaryotic cells typically have a size range of:
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells are usually between 10 and 100 micrometers wide, while prokaryotes are 1–10 micrometers.

questions.question: The term 'eukaryotic' is derived from Greek words meaning:
questions.explanation: 'Eu' means true and 'karyon' means kernel (nucleus), so eukaryotic means 'true nucleus'.

questions.question: The term 'prokaryotic' is derived from Greek words meaning:
questions.explanation: 'Pro' means before and 'karyon' means nucleus, reflecting the earlier evolution of prokaryotic cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells for photosynthesis but are absent in animal cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is found in animal cells but NOT in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Centrioles are found in animal cells and anchor microtubules during cell division; plant cells lack centrioles.

questions.question: Lysosomes are found in animal cells but are generally absent in:
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are typically found in animal cells but are absent in plant cells.

questions.question: A microscope that uses lenses to bend light and magnify objects is called a:
questions.explanation: A light microscope uses lenses to bend light toward the eye, making objects appear larger.

questions.question: Why is iodine solution used when observing onion cells under a microscope?
options: To stain the cell structures for better visibility
questions.correctAnswer: To stain the cell structures for better visibility
questions.explanation: Iodine stains cell components (like the nucleus), making them more visible under the microscope.

questions.question: When preparing a wet mount, the coverslip should be lowered at an angle of about 45 degrees to:
questions.explanation: Lowering the coverslip at an angle helps prevent air bubbles that would obscure features under the microscope.

questions.question: What stain is commonly used to observe cheek (animal) cells under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Methylene blue dye is used to stain cheek cells, making the nucleus and other structures more visible.

questions.question: Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from a region of:
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the passive movement of molecules down a concentration gradient, from high to low concentration.

questions.question: Passive transport differs from active transport because passive transport:
questions.explanation: Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without using energy.

questions.question: Osmosis is a special case of diffusion involving the movement of:
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.question: In osmosis, water moves from a region of:
options: high solute concentration to low solute concentration
high water concentration to low water concentration
low water concentration to high water concentration
questions.correctAnswer: high water concentration to low water concentration
questions.explanation: Water moves from an area of higher water concentration (dilute solution) to lower water concentration (concentrated solution).

questions.question: A solution with a high concentration of solute and low concentration of water is called:
questions.explanation: A hypertonic solution has more solute and less water compared to the cell's interior.

questions.question: A solution with a low concentration of solute and high concentration of water is called:
questions.explanation: A hypotonic solution has less solute and more water compared to the cell's interior.

questions.question: When a cell and its surroundings have equal solute and water concentrations, the solution is called:
questions.explanation: In an isotonic solution, water diffuses into and out of the cell at the same rate.

questions.question: When a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, the cell:
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution, water leaves the plant cell, causing the plasma membrane to shrink away from the cell wall (plasmolysis).

questions.question: When an animal cell is placed in a hypotonic solution, the cell:
questions.explanation: Animal cells lack a cell wall, so in a hypotonic solution, water enters and the cell may burst, a process called hemolysis.

questions.question: The process where red blood cells burst due to excessive water intake is called:
questions.explanation: Hemolysis occurs when red blood cells take in too much water in a hypotonic solution and burst.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect the rate of diffusion?
questions.explanation: Diffusion rate is affected by concentration gradient, temperature, mass of molecule, distance, and surface area, not color.

questions.question: Active transport is the movement of molecules from:
options: high to low concentration (no energy needed)
low to high concentration (no energy needed)
questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient, requiring energy from respiration.

questions.question: An example of active transport in plants is:
questions.explanation: Root hairs use active transport to absorb mineral ions from the soil against a concentration gradient.

questions.question: Tiny projections on the surface of some cells that increase surface area for absorption are called:
questions.explanation: Microvilli are tiny projections that increase the absorbing surface area, found in kidney and intestinal cells.

questions.question: A group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function is called a:
questions.explanation: Tissues are groups of similar cells that act as a functional unit.

questions.question: An organ is composed of:
questions.explanation: Organs are made of several different tissues grouped to perform a special function.

questions.question: The correct order of biological organization from simplest to most complex is:
options: cell → organ → tissue → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
tissue → cell → organ → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ system → organ → organism
questions.correctAnswer: cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems form an organism.

questions.question: Beyond the individual organism, biological organization extends to:
questions.explanation: Populations of the same species form communities, which interact in ecosystems, all part of the biosphere.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an organ in flowering plants?
questions.explanation: In flowering plants, roots, stems, and leaves are organs; epidermis and xylem are tissues.

questions.question: Unicellular protozoans like amoeba prevent bursting in freshwater using:
questions.explanation: Contractile vacuoles expel excess water from the cell, preventing bursting in hypotonic freshwater environments.

questions.question: Which two structures are used for locomotion in unicellular organisms?
questions.explanation: Cilia (short, hair-like) and flagella (long, thread-like) are organelles for locomotion in unicellular organisms.

questions.question: What happens when a cell containing 1% sodium chloride is placed in seawater containing 10% sodium chloride?
options: Water moves from seawater into the cell
Water moves from the cell into seawater
questions.correctAnswer: Water moves from the cell into seawater
questions.explanation: The seawater is hypertonic (higher solute concentration), so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

questions.question: The site where new ribosomes are made is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a darker area within the nucleus where new ribosomes are produced.

questions.question: Turgor pressure in plants is important for:
options: retaining upright posture and extended leaves
questions.correctAnswer: retaining upright posture and extended leaves
questions.explanation: Turgor pressure from water pressing outwards on the cell wall keeps plants upright and leaves extended.
